newsitem.title: UK: Sedgwick plans new corporate client service.
newsitem.headline: Sedgwick plans new corporate client service.

text.p: Sedgwick Group, the UK-based insurance broker, said on Tuesday it aimed, from January, to offer some of its corporate clients a new centralised way of conducting business.
The move is designed to reduce administration and make prices more competitive, while making use of computer technology to improve communication.

In a UK market which has become increasingly competitive and where rates remain stubbornly low, insurers and brokers alike have been forced to look at ways of shoring up a deterioration in margins other than raising what policyholders are charged.

Sedgwick's UK general retail arm, which sells insurance to British corporate customers, said a pilot scheme centralising broking and processing was expected to be offered to a particular segment of its client base from January.
It will be targeted at "middle market" corporate clients in the UK -- a small proportion of the entire group's client base.

Dedicated teams from Sedgwick and the insurers will work from the group's Manchester office, providing underwriting and claims handling for those customers. Clients will use laptop computers for communicating with the Manchester office.

"The rationale is that the inland market is extremely fierce, margins are tight and price is the principal factor when choosing a broker," UK marketing director for Sedgwick UK Risk Services Gary Stott told Reuters.

"Technology will form a big part of it but that's really to get the communication going between people looking after and servicing clients in our branch infrastructure with a central site where the broking will be done with insurers," he said.
Stott added that there were no plans yet to extend the service, but suggested the industry as a whole may be heading towards similar ways of doing business.
Sedgwick is one of six international brokers which owns the World Insurance Network (WIN), a company planning to launch electronic commerce services for the global insurance industry.

The insurance broker earlier on Tuesday reported nine month pre-tax profits of 80.4 million stg, up from 76.5 million, but noted that an industry-wide reduction in rates continued to pressurise most parts of its business.
Analysts said the gains at pre-tax level were in part a result of Sedgwick's efforts to reduce interest payments, which shrank by three million stg to 7.7 million.
